findings.entity:
Southland Holdings, Inc. (Other / unclassified, tier canary)
THESIS: CONFIRMED and escalated beyond "canary" — this entity is already-distressed, not merely fragile. The scan flagged it on a leverage/refi/carry signature, but the real fracture is contract-claim/judgment risk feeding a balance-sheet collapse. In FY2025 Southland posted a $306.5M net loss on $772.2M revenue (revenue down 21.2% YoY) with an EBITDA loss of $191.4M. An adverse trial-court ruling on the Washington State Convention Center (WSCC) project drove a $135.8M unfavorable adjustment (derecognized $40.3M contract assets, cut $6.4M retainage, booked an $89.1M accrued judgment liability), pushing total stockholders' equity to a deficit of $(140.9)M at 12/31/2025 (from +$163.7M a year earlier), deepening to $(160.6)M by 3/31/2026. The company breached its credit agreement; its sureties (Zurich et al.) have effectively replaced the prior term-loan lender (Callodine), advanced ~$116-139M under General Indemnity Agreements to keep bonded jobs running, and WAIVED all defaults, covenant violations, and quarterly principal/monthly interest payments until maturity — i.e., the company is being kept alive by its bonding companies, who now sit ahead of equity and effectively control the capital structure. Equity trades at ~$0.65-1.07 (off a $5.34 52-wk high), market cap ~$58M. This is a going-concern situation in substance even where the audit conclusion language is being managed via the surety forbearance to May 13, 2027. NOT mispriced as a hidden short — the market has already marked the equity to near-zero; the fragility is REAL and largely realized.

findings.entity:
Hyperscale Data, Inc. (Data center / AI infra, tier canary)
THESIS: This is a genuine canary and it is ALREADY DISTRESSED, not mispriced-pending-discovery. The FY2025 10-K (filed Apr 2026, auditor Marcum LLP) carries an explicit going-concern qualification citing a "significant working capital deficiency" and recurring losses. The economy-wide scan's framing is directionally right but the magnitudes are artifacts: actual interest-bearing debt is ~$105M (not $0.33B) — Notes payable $91.2M + related-party NP $0.9M + convertible notes $13.4M at 3/31/26. The "$0.33B gross" figure almost certainly double-counts gross facility issuances and rolled/converted/repaid tranches across the year (the company churned dozens of short-dated notes — e.g., $51.2M gross notes-payable proceeds AND $57.3M repayments in 2025 alone). The real fragility is structural and self-evident: (1) Going concern + $767M accumulated deficit at 3/31/26, growing ~$32M PER QUARTER. (2) Cash burn: $62.5M used in operations FY2025 vs only $13.1M unrestricted cash at year-end ($36.2M restricted is largely pledged Bitcoin collateral) — a sub-3-month operating runway absent continuous capital raising. (3) Survival is 100% dilution-funded: $156.3M of financing inflows in 2025 ($125M common-stock sales + $32.4M Series B preferred + convertibles), and the share count exploded from 323M to 370M Class A shares in a SINGLE quarter (Q1 2026), authorized Class A raised from 500M to 2.5 BILLION shares on 4/16/26 — classic death-spiral mechanics with VWAP/floor-price convertibles. (4) The flagship $68.75M AGREE construction loan (~65-75% of notes payable) is in technical default: required April 2026 principal payments and ~$2M interest reserves remained UNFUNDED as of the Q1 filing (lenders have granted forbearance/waivers but not waived the default). (5) Preferred stack is a permanent cash drain: 13.00% Series D and 10.00% Series E perpetual preferreds plus a 9.5% Series H ($100M facility with Ault & Co.); $8.6M preferred dividends paid in 2025, $2.5M in Q1 2026, against negative operating cash flow. The max-coupon 15% signature is real (15% term notes "in default," SJC 15% convertible, and effective rates up to 36-77% once OID/forbearance fees are amortized — the 12% Ault term note carries a 77% EFFECTIVE rate), confirming distressed-priced paper. Coverage is deeply negative; this entity does not generate cash to service obligations and is solvent only quarter-to-quarter via equity issuance into a falling stock.

findings.entity: Humacyte, Inc. (NASDAQ: HUMA; CIK 0001818382)
findings.fragility_thesis: CONFIRMED canary, by cash-flow mechanics rather than by the scan's debt headline. This is a single-product, cash-incinerating commercial-stage biotech whose obligations vastly outrun its revenue: FY2025 total revenue was only ~$2.0M (of which ~$1.4M was 61 Symvess units) against quarterly operating cash burn of roughly $25-29M (Q1 2025 op cash burn ~$28.6M; Q1 2026 ~$25.1M), a ~$744.5M accumulated deficit at Mar-31-2026, and explicit going-concern doubt in successive 2025/2026 filings. Cash collapsed from $62.8M (+$50.4M restricted) at Q1-2025 to just $19.8M total cash/restricted at Q3-2025, forcing a December 2025 venture-debt rescue and repeated dilutive equity raises. The fragility is funding-runway and dilution risk: survival depends entirely on continuously tapping equity (ATM/registered directs at $0.80-$1.05/share) and milestone-gated debt tranches while a clinically-niche product ramps slowly. Importantly, the scan's $293.9M 'gross debt' is a data artifact / facility-maximum aggregation — actual drawn term debt is only ~$35.9M (Q1 2026). The REAL distress signals are the 11.50% venture-debt coupon (genuine, not a penalty rate), the going-concern qualification, and the equity collapse to sub-$1 with massive share-count growth (159M shares Sep-2025 to 222M by May-2026).

THESIS: CONFIRMED canary, already-distressed and failing in real time — but the scan MIS-SIZED it by ~10x. This is a sub-$25M-revenue microcap that has burned through nearly all its equity ($981K stockholders' equity and $393K cash at Sep 30, 2025) and is being involuntarily removed from a major exchange THIS WEEK. On June 11, 2026 NYSE American Regulatory Staff determined PMNT failed to regain compliance with the minimum stockholders'-equity standard (Sec. 1003(a)(ii)) within the maximum 18-month plan period; the board elected to move to OTCQB; common stock is to be suspended from NYSE American the week of June 15, 2026 (today is June 13, 2026). FY24 audit (Weinberg & Co.) carried a going-concern qualification; FY25 net loss ~$16M on $21.5M revenue (-12% YoY) driven partly by the bankruptcy of its largest wholesale customer, Matches Fashion. The fragility is REAL and acute: chronic operating losses, negative-to-trivial equity, multi-round emergency financing, repeated insider-loan maturity extensions, and a 15% distressed convertible note. HOWEVER, the genuine threat is equity/liquidity destruction and delisting, NOT a debt cliff: total gross debt is small (~$12-17M, see below), and the company posted its first profitable quarter in Q3 FY26 (net income $93K, gross margin ~64%) and repaid short-term borrowings — so an operational survival path exists if the new $10M secured revolver and equity raises hold. Net: high-severity equity/listing fragility, moderate credit fragility, low systemic relevance.

findings.entity:
SunPower Inc. (Other / unclassified, tier canary)
THESIS: CONFIRMED CANARY — already-distressed, not mispriced-but-fine. The entity has an explicit GOING-CONCERN qualification in its FY2025 10-K ("substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern"). Liquidity is critically thin: only ~$9.5M cash (Q1'26) / $9.6M (FY25) against ~$24.3M current debt and ~$56.6M accrued/other current liabilities — i.e. near-term obligations exceed cash by ~8x. The company is burning ~$13–19M/quarter operating loss (FY25 net loss $40.6M; accumulated deficit $456.7M) and only reaches its own claimed cash-flow breakeven at ~$96M quarterly revenue vs ~$73M actual in Q1'26. It is deferring cash interest by offering stock/bonus shares in lieu of cash coupons on its 12% and 7% convertible notes for the Jul-2026 and Jan-2027 payments (a PIK-style cash-conservation move = textbook distress). It required emergency capital (April 2026 $41M 10% convert; Fortis Capital incremental May 2026) explicitly to "carry us through 2026." Layer on a TRIPLE restatement (Q1–Q3 2025), material weaknesses across all four COSO components, double-booked revenue removed ($308.8M→$300M), and late 12b-25 filings for both the 10-K and Q1'26 10-Q. This entity fails first.

findings.entity: NextNRG, Inc. (Nasdaq: NXXT; CIK 0001817004; formerly EzFill Holdings)
findings.fragility_thesis: CONFIRMED canary — already-distressed, not merely flagged. This is a cash-starved micro-cap funding operations through a continuous stream of expensive, short-dated, partly related-party paper. As of 3/31/2026: cash of only ~$208K against ~$34.3M total liabilities, a ~$22.0M stockholders' DEFICIT, current ratio ~0.1, and a Q1 net loss of ~$10.8M (FY net losses far larger). The auditor (M&K CPAs) issued an explicit going-concern paragraph for FY2025. Revenue is growing fast (Q1 2026 ~$21.1M, +29% YoY; FY ~+195%) but gross margins are thin (mobile fueling) and the company is deeply cash-flow negative, so growth widens the funding hole rather than closing it. Survival depends entirely on serial dilution and high-cost secured/convertible debt — including merchant cash advances and notes carrying 18% DEFAULT interest plus 150%-of-principal acceleration penalties — and on CEO/Chairman Michael Farkas repeatedly lending money and then swapping it for stock (debt-for-equity at $1.67 in Sept 2025, $1.04 in Nov 2025). On top of solvency stress, NXXT received a 3/16/2026 Nasdaq notice for failing the $1.00 minimum bid (compliance deadline 9/14/2026), so a reverse split or delisting is likely, which would impair its only real funding channel (equity/convertibles). IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the scan: the ~$0.14B "gross debt" is a data artifact — the local extraction double/triple-counts the same notes (same instrument captured as both a 'bond' and a 'debt_facility' row and across multiple amendment 8-Ks; e.g., the $2.95M note x4, $8.85M x2, $1.724M Leviston x5). True interest-bearing debt is on the order of ~$20-22M (related-party notes ~$11.5M + other notes ~$10.1M at Q1 2026). Likewise the 18% "max coupon" is a penalty/default rate, not the running coupon (stated coupons are ~10-12%). The fragility is real and severe, but it is small-dollar (tens of millions), so the systemic-cascade angle is negligible — this is a first-to-fail canary, not a node.

findings.entity:

findings.entity: X.AI LLC / X.AI Corp (xAI) — operating subsidiary of X.AI Holdings Corp.; since Feb 2, 2026 a subsidiary of Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (SpaceX) via the xAI Merger
findings.fragility_thesis: The seed flag ("~$20B gross debt, ~$20B due <=2027, max coupon 2.0%, front-loaded refi wall, 1 non-recourse SPV") is a DATA ARTIFACT on the headline numbers but points at a REAL, filing-confirmed fragility that has been transferred up to the parent. Corrections: (1) The 2.0% coupon is wrong — xAI's actual paper was a $3.0B tranche of 12.50% Senior Secured Notes due June 2030 plus a 12.5%-area Fixed Rate Loan and a SOFR+725bp Floating Rate Loan (the ~12.5% level is textbook distressed-borrower pricing). The ~2-4.58% the scanner likely latched onto is the SpaceX-level refinanced bridge, not xAI. (2) The '$20B due <=2027' refi wall no longer sits at xAI: on March 5, 2026 ALL of xAI's funded debt (Fixed Rate Loan, Floating Rate Loan, $3B 12.5% Notes) plus X's two term loans were extinguished and rolled into the $20,000M unsecured SpaceX Bridge Loan (March 2026; matures Sep 2, 2027, two 3-mo extensions to Mar 2028) at the SPaceX level, triggering a $1,526M loss on extinguishment and a $518M prepayment penalty. The bridge must be repaid within 6 months of SpaceX's IPO (which opened June 12, 2026), so the refi wall is real but is now SpaceX's, with X.AI LLC as a joint-and-several guarantor. (3) The genuine hidden-leverage / ring-fenced signature is REAL and filing-confirmed: the Valor Equity Partners GPU equipment leases — three agreements aggregating $20.2B of cash payments ($6,986M + $6,633M + $6,587M) where an xAI subsidiary (CTC) leases Nvidia GPUs from Valor entities (controlled by SpaceX director Antonio Gracias). PwC ruled these 'failed sale-leasebacks,' forcing ~$9.9B of related debt onto SpaceX's balance sheet ($455M current + $4,052M + $5,365M). This is related-party, GPU-collateralized, SpaceX-guaranteed financing that behaves like secured debt, not operating leases. NET READ: xAI standalone is deeply cash-negative (FY2025: ~$6.4B operating loss on ~$3.2B revenue; Q3 widening to ~$1.46B net loss/qtr; ~$1B/mo burn; ~$0.5B ARR vs ~$30B annualized capex run-rate) and could not service 12.5% debt on its own cash flows — it was a distressed credit. But it is NO LONGER a standalone refi-wall canary: the fragility was absorbed by SpaceX, which de-risked the coupon (12.5% -> ~4.58% bridge) and now carries the consolidated obligation and the Valor failed-SLB debt. Judge xAI as a structurally insolvent operating unit whose solvency is now entirely a function of (a) SpaceX's IPO-funded balance sheet and (b) continued equity infusions (Nvidia up to $2B equity into the separate Colossus 2 SPV; $7.5B equity / $12.5B debt SPV is additive, off-the-refinanced-stack future leverage).

FY2025 actuals: $321.1M total debt, $119.7M net debt, falling to $42.4M net debt by Q1 2026 after the May-2025 exchange (~$132M of 2026 notes swapped into $100.8M of 8.75% second-lien notes due 2030) and ongoing bond repurchases — so the leverage(0.12)/refi(0.03) signals are LOW and largely self-cured. Riley Financial) — B&W's LARGEST SHAREHOLDER and a related-party LENDER (the second-lien notes share collateral with the B. Riley junior secured note). Bryant Riley sits on both the B&W cap table and Base Electron's board, and allegedly sold stock (~$10.4M) into the spike. Multiple securities-fraud class actions (Pomerantz; Levi & Korsinsky) allege the contract value was inflated and that BRC was provided "exit liquidity." The canary signature: an obscure, chronically cash-burning small-cap whose survival narrative and equity value rest on a single, contingent, related-party-tangled contract — it re-rates (and de-rates) on contract credibility, not on operations.

findings.entity: Rapid Micro Biosystems, Inc. (NASDAQ: RPID; CIK 0001380106)
findings.fragility_thesis: GENUINE CANARY, but the scan flagged the wrong mechanism. The scan's debt-driven thesis (~$0.47B gross debt, distressed 11.5% coupon, circular financing) is almost entirely a DATA ARTIFACT — actual drawn debt is ~$20M. The real fragility is CASH BURN / RUNWAY, which a leverage-centric lens understates. RPID is a chronically loss-making nano-cap ($33.6M FY25 revenue, ~$47M FY25 net loss, ~20% gross margin) whose cash fell $50.7M (Dec-24) -> $39M (Dec-25) -> ~$23M (Mar-26), i.e. ~$14-16M burned in Q1-26 alone (Q1-26 net loss $14.3M on $8.0M revenue). At ~$23M cash against a ~$14M/quarter loss, the cash-only runway is roughly 4-5 quarters. Management's 'at least 12 months' assurance leans on milestone-gated, lender-discretion Trinity tranches ($25M undrawn) that may not unlock, and on the dilutive equity ATM/shelf. findings.entity: Arbor Realty Trust Inc (NYSE: ABR) [CIK 0001253986]
findings.fragility_thesis: Genuinely stressed, but NOT for the flagged reason. The "counterparty concentration HHI 1.00" seed is a DATA ARTIFACT — ABR is a diversified lender across thousands of multifamily/CRE borrowers and multiple repo counterparties (JPMorgan and others); the only true single-name relationship is the Fannie Mae DUS channel, which is a contingent loss-share/servicing obligation, not gross-debt concentration. REJECT the literal concentration thesis. The REAL fragility is a credit-cycle + financing-structure problem in the Structured (balance-sheet bridge) book: (1) Credit deterioration — non-performing assets ~$1B, roughly 8% of the portfolio as of Q1 2026, after ~$1.9B of multifamily bridge-loan modifications (maturity extensions + temporary rate relief), a textbook 'extend-and-pretend' that masks but does not cure underwater floating-rate multifamily collateral. (2) Earnings/dividend collapse — common dividend cut from $0.30 to $0.17 in Q1 2026 (down ~60% from the 2023 $0.43 peak); Q1 2026 GAAP EPS $0.00 (net income $0.6M vs $30.4M prior-year); distributable earnings only $0.07/sh, dragged by $22.9M of net realized losses on legacy assets — distributable earnings now barely cover even the reduced dividend. (3) Financing-structure migration RAISES, not lowers, run-risk: ABR is unwinding non-recourse, non-mark-to-market legacy CLOs (e.g., $787M CLO 17 redeemed) and pushing assets into repo facilities at higher leverage (~76% vs ~68%); even though new facilities are marketed as ~88% non-recourse, the residual recourse + the inherent mark-to-market nature of repo reintroduces margin-call exposure that the CLO structure was specifically designed to avoid. (4) Overhang — active Viceroy Research fraud campaign (off-balance-sheet REO financing allegations) plus reported DOJ/FBI inquiry and shareholder litigation; unresolved, but a real headline/financing-access risk. Net: not an imminent insolvency, but a deteriorating-credit mid-cap mREIT whose earnings power and book value are eroding and whose move toward recourse/MTM funding increases tail fragility.

findings.entity: AMC Entertainment Holdings, Inc. (AMC; CIK 0001411579)
findings.fragility_thesis: FLAG DIRECTION CONFIRMED, SEED NUMBERS REJECTED AS ARTIFACTS. findings.entity: ContextLogic Holdings Inc. (OTCQB: LOGC; formerly Wish / ContextLogic Inc., NASDAQ: WISH)
findings.fragility_thesis: The scan's headline flag is a DATA ARTIFACT, and on its own cash flows this entity is NOT acutely fragile. The "~$2.38B gross debt" does not exist: actual funded debt is a $215M secured term loan + $25M revolver ($240M facility; ~$210M long-term debt at Q1 2026). The $2.38B figure is a size-metric over-count that conflated the company's ~$2.7-2.9B NOL tax ASSET (a deferred-tax attribute, not a liability) with debt. The "10% coupon" is REAL but is ordinary sponsor-LBO pricing, not a penalty rate: the term loan is SOFR+4.00-4.50% (~9.4% at YE2025), and the BC Partners preferred units pay 4.00% stepping to 8.00% post-acquisition. The "circular/concentration" flags are also real structure, not noise: BC Partners (via its credit arm) supplies BOTH preferred equity and credit, Abrams Capital is the largest equity holder (40.72%) and a roll-over seller, and the entire operating business is ONE salt plant. The genuine — but moderate — fragility is structural, not a debt wall: (1) single-asset concentration (100% of operating cash flow from one Watkins Glen facility; any operational disruption hits coverage directly); (2) moderate leverage ~4.5x net of the term loan vs US Salt 2025 EBITDA $47.9M, with interest coverage only ~2.4x (EBITDA $47.9M / ~$20M cash interest); (3) parent liquidity was drawn down from ~$217M cash at acquisition to ~$12M at Q1 2026, so the cash cushion that made this a 'shell with optionality' is now largely consumed; (4) the equity is a levered, illiquid OTCQB Up-C bet whose thesis depends on monetizing NOLs against future acquired earnings. This is a sponsor-backed micro-cap LBO, not a distressed-debt canary. Severity is moderate (single-asset cyclical leverage), NOT high/already-distressed. The scan should reclassify the debt figure.
findings.false_positive_reason: The scan's HEADLINE is a false positive caused by deal-extraction over-count: the same $215M term loan + $25M revolver was ingested 7 times across S-1/S-1/A/8-K/commitment-letter/10-K/10-Q and combined with mis-parsed dollar strings, inflating ~$240M of facilities into a $2.38B/12-deal 'debt wall.' findings.entity:
BTCS Inc. (Other / unclassified, tier canary)
THESIS: The scan's "18% coupon / distressed tranche" flag is a DATA ARTIFACT and should be rejected as stated: BTCS's senior secured convertible notes carry a STATED 6% coupon with a 5% OID and a 198% conversion premium ($13.00 conv. price) — these were issued at a premium, the opposite of distressed pricing. The 18% is a DEFAULT/PENALTY interest rate triggered only on an Event of Default (BTCS's older 2016 notes used 24% default; recent notes ~18%), not a market-cleared yield. So "distressed-priced tranche up to 18%" is wrong. HOWEVER, this entity IS genuinely fragile, just via a different mechanism the credit-coupon lens misses entirely. The true fragility is a crypto-collateralized leverage loop: ~$61.5M of ETH-backed DeFi loans (primarily Aave USDT against ETH collateral) plus ~$11.8M net convertibles, sitting on only ~$1.5M of corporate CASH (12/31/25) against ETH that is intrinsically volatile. The company borrows stablecoins against ETH to buy more ETH — a reflexive, self-amplifying long. A sharp ETH drawdown simultaneously (a) collapses collateral value toward Aave's ~80% liquidation threshold, risking automated on-chain liquidation of the ETH at the worst moment, (b) drives the convertibles deeper out-of-the-money so they stay debt rather than converting to equity, and (c) crushes equity/ATM capacity, the lifeline that funds the ~$1.5M-cash operating shortfall (FY25 net loss $33.4M, incl. $15.7M unrealized digital-asset loss; thin $2.0M gross profit at 12% margin). This is a textbook canary: tiny, obscure, with a fully procyclical liability structure that fails FIRST in an ETH downcycle via margin liquidation, not via a coupon.
SEVERITY CLAIMED: moderate
DISTRESS INDICATORS CLAIMED: FY2025 net loss of $33.4M, including $15.7M unrealized digital-asset loss; Corporate cash collapsed to ~$1.5M at 12/31/25 despite $200M+ raised — operations not self-funding; Gross margin compressed to 12% (from 23% in 2024) on thin $2.0M gross profit; Cash+digital assets fell from ~$242M (Jul 2025) to ~$126M (Mar 2026) as ETH fell and debt stayed — net asset value contracting; Funding model is reflexive: borrowing stablecoins against ETH to buy more ETH (self-amplifying leverage); Reliance on continuous ATM equity dilution to fund the cash-burning operating business; Convertibles deeply out-of-the-money ($13.00 strike) — will not convert to equity in a downturn, stay as senior secured debt; Automated Aave liquidation risk if ETH draws down ~40-50% toward the ~80% liquidation threshold

Attack it: are the cash flows actually adequate? Is the high coupon a one-off / penalty / mis-extraction? Already refinanced or covenant-cured? findings.entity:
NEXPOINT DIVERSIFIED REAL ESTATE TRUST (Other / unclassified, tier canary)
THESIS: REAL but NARROW canary, and the original scan numbers are wrong. Filing-verified (10-Q period 2026-03-31, 10-K FY2025): total debt is ~$284M gross / $278M net (scan said ~$0.15B — understated), and near-term maturities are ~$218M not ~$0 (scan said ~$0.00B ≤2027). The fragility is a concentrated single-asset refinancing wall, not a coupon-distress or solvency story. The Cityplace office tower carries $137.0M of debt (senior at ~6%, B-notes/mezz at ~10%) whose maturity has been serially deferred on a short leash by the lender: March 8 2026 → May 8 2026 → July 8 2026. Management states it can give "no assurance" the lender extends further, that "finding an alternative source of funding is necessary," and explicitly reserves the contractual right to SURRENDER the property to the lender in lieu of repayment (limited-recourse loan). findings.entity: Sabre GLBL Inc. (operating subsidiary of Sabre Corporation, NASDAQ: SABR; CIK 0001597033)
findings.fragility_thesis: The economy-wide scan's headline flag — a "front-loaded refi wall of ~$4B due <=2027" — is STALE and should be REJECTED. Through 2023-2025 Sabre executed one of the most aggressive liability-management campaigns in the leveraged-credit market (it literally pioneered the "pari plus" double-dip structure in June 2023). As of YE2025, >90% of debt matures in 2029 or later; the residual 2027 notes ($91.6M of 8.625%) are being redeemed 1-March-2026 at 102.156. There is no near-term maturity wall. The REAL and persistent fragility is the INTEREST BURDEN created by that refi, not refinancing risk. Coupons run 10.75%-11.25% on ~$3.24B of senior secured notes; FY2025 interest expense was ~$441M against ~$585M pro-forma Adjusted EBITDA (cash-interest coverage barely ~1.3x EBITDA, and EBITDA is well below true cash interest once capex and working capital are netted). Free cash flow was NEGATIVE $192M in FY2025 (incl. $227M PIK interest pushed through operating cash flow during the refi) and is guided to NEGATIVE ~$70M in FY2026, with management projecting positive FCF only in 2027 — and even that is fragile, leaning on an "inflation offset" restructuring/severance program. Bernstein projects leverage stays >5x net debt/EBITDA into the 2030s. So this entity is NOT a refi-wall canary; it is a high-coupon, negative-FCF, structurally-subordinated grind that depends on travel-demand growth (which is currently positive: revenue +8% YoY) to outrun a punitive interest stack. The structural-subordination/ring-fencing flags are GENUINE: Sabre Financial Borrower LLC is an unrestricted-subsidiary "pari plus" vehicle ($1.0B 11.125% notes due 2029, plus an earlier Centerbridge-led $700M term loan) with foreign-subsidiary guarantees capped at $400M of separate collateral — a creditor-on-creditor priming structure that subordinates legacy holders. Net: moderate, improving-at-the-margin but still over-levered; the mispricing is in the OPPOSITE direction the scan implied — duration risk has been term-extended away, leaving a slow-bleed coupon-coverage problem that only a sustained EBITDA ramp resolves.

findings.entity: NextDecade Corp (NASDAQ: NEXT) — parent of Rio Grande LNG, LLC (RGLNG), Brownsville TX export terminal
findings.fragility_thesis: Genuine but STRUCTURALLY MISCLASSIFIED fragility — confirm with a major caveat. The scan's $28.85B "gross debt" is real but ~$27B+ of it is NON-RECOURSE PROJECT FINANCE ring-fenced inside the RGLNG SPV tower (23 non-recourse + 8 SPV flags are accurate, not artifacts): $11.6B Phase 1 senior secured bank facilities + private-placement notes (6.58%/6.72% — investment-grade-priced, NOT distressed), plus ~$3.85B Train 4 and ~$3.59B Train 5 credit agreements. The 13.0% max coupon is REAL and load-bearing but is NOT a distressed bond — it is the $600M SuperFinCo equity-bridge term loan (PIK until ~1yr after Train 5 completion, callable at par Sept 2030), a CORPORATE-LEVEL RECOURSE instrument used to fund NextDecade's own equity contribution without diluting common shares. That is the true fragility node: the parent is funding its minority equity stake with expensive PIK recourse debt against an asset that produces zero cash until 2027 and from which NextDecade receives only ~20.8% of Phase 1 cash flows (it is a minority economic holder of the project it controls/consolidates). The actual fragility is NOT a leverage/refi wall — near-term project amortization is minimal pre-COD — it is PARENT LIQUIDITY/RUNWAY: going-concern substantial-doubt language persists in the FY2025 10-K, only ~$143M unrestricted cash at 3/31/2026, recurring ~$130-160M/qtr net losses, financed by serial equity issuance (ATM/shelf) and PIK accrual. The entity is fragile to EXECUTION (Train 1 schedule/cost) and CAPITAL-MARKETS ACCESS, not to a classic debt cliff. If construction stays on time and offtake SPAs (TotalEnergies 5.4Mtpa+, Shell 2Mtpa, ENN, others; 20-yr take-or-pay) convert to cash flow on schedule, the recourse PIK is refinanced/repaid from distributions and the structure de-risks sharply.

findings.entity: Venture Global, Inc. (NYSE: VG) [CIK 0002007855]
findings.fragility_thesis: The scan's debt/leverage/carry flags are largely artifacts and do NOT make VG fragile: the operating business is strongly cash-generative (FY2025 revenue $13.77B, income from operations $5.16B, net income $2.73B; Q1'26 revenue $4.6B, adj. EBITDA $1.4B, FY2026 EBITDA guide raised to $8.2-8.5B) and the bulk of debt is non-recourse project-level financing. The REAL fragility is litigation, not the balance sheet. VG built its early revenue by selling ~3 years of 'commissioning' cargoes through affiliate VG Commodities (the 'circular 0.30' signature = intercompany excess-capacity SPAs) on the spot market instead of declaring commercial operations and delivering to fixed-fee offtakers. That triggered arbitrations: an ICC tribunal found VGCP breached its post-COD SPA / 'Reasonable and Prudent Operator' duty to BP (BP seeking ~$3.7B, potentially >$6B incl. interest/costs); Shell obtained a partial liability award and seeks $6.7B-$7.4B (VG challenging in NY court); Edison settling Q2'26. Combined disclosed claims (~$10B+ gross sought) approach a full year of EBITDA, and the 10-K discloses these as 'reasonably possible' with no quantified accrual — that is the under-reserved, potentially-mispriced hole. Exposure sits primarily at the Calcasieu (VGCP) project level but contract/cross-default and reputational/refinancing channels can reach the parent.

findings.entity: Bausch & Lomb Corp (NYSE/TSX: BLCO)
findings.fragility_thesis: The standalone-insolvency read is REJECTED, but a real STRUCTURAL fragility is CONFIRMED — it just isn't where the scan pointed. BLCO is a growing, cash-generative operator (FY2025 revenue $5.10B +6%, adj. EBITDA ex-IPR&D $891M, operating cash flow $283M) with NO near-term maturity wall: the June 2025 refinancing termed out all 2027 maturities into 2028/2030/2031, so the scan's "near-term ≤2027 = $0.00B" is correct and is the single most de-risking fact. Leverage is elevated (net debt/EBITDA ~5.2x on the $891M ex-IPR&D base; ~7.2x on the lower IPR&D-inclusive/trailing base) and BLCO posts a GAAP net loss ($360M FY2025) driven by D&A, IPR&D and ~$421M interest — but coverage (~$891M EBITDA vs ~$421M interest ≈ 2.1x) and a long runway mean this is a slow-burn balance sheet, not a fragile one, on a standalone basis. The GENUINE fragility is RELATIONAL/STRUCTURAL: BLCO is held as an UNRESTRICTED SUBSIDIARY of parent Bausch Health (BHC, ~88% owner), which is itself ~6.1x levered with its own near-term maturities and Valeant-era securities-fraud + Xifaxan-exclusivity overhangs. BHC's entire deleveraging and arguably its SOLVENCY case depends on monetizing its BLCO stake (~$8.75B at ~$25/sh). The long-promised separation is gated on 'targeted leverage ratios' and carries explicit FRAUDULENT-CONVEYANCE risk (distributing BLCO value to BHC shareholders over BHC creditors). So BLCO's mispricing is not credit-insolvency — it is event/structural: a healthy asset whose equity and the separation timeline are hostage to a distressed parent's restructuring, creditor litigation, and unrestricted-sub covenant maneuvering. THE SCAN'S NUMERIC FLAGS ARE LARGELY ARTIFACTS: (1) 'max coupon 2.8%' is FALSE — BLCO's real debt yields ~8% (8.375% 2028 notes; SOFR/EURIBOR+~3.875% floating; $421M interest on ~$5B implies ~8% effective), so 2.8% is a parsing error. (2) 'gross debt ~$13.43B' overstates BLCO — standalone principal is ~$5.0B; $13B is BHC-consolidated/segment contamination. (3) The 'concentration/circular/related-party' signature is the ONE real flag and correctly fingerprints the BHC parent dependency, not a customer/supplier issue.

findings.entity: Applied Digital Corp. (NASDAQ: APLD; CIK 0001144879)
findings.fragility_thesis: The scan's headline ($26.75B gross debt, $9.30B near-term) is a DATA ARTIFACT and should be rejected at roughly 5-6x overstatement. Actual on-balance-sheet gross debt was ~$2.61B at 11/30/2025 with NET debt of only ~$488M (cash + restricted ~$2.12B). Pro forma for the March 2026 $2.15B ComputeCo 2 notes, gross debt is ~$4.8B; if the June 2026 $1.59B Polaris Forge 1 building-4 notes close, ~$6.4B — still a fraction of $26.75B. The $26.75B almost certainly sums NON-DEBT items as debt: ~$16B of CONTRACTED FUTURE LEASE REVENUE (CoreWeave ~$11B + Polaris Forge 2 hyperscaler ~$5B over ~15yr), plus the $5.0B Macquarie PERPETUAL PREFERRED + 15%-common commitment in the HPC subsidiary (equity/minority interest, not debt, and largely undrawn), plus the real ~$4.5-6.4B of notes and the $550M revolver. The 'max 9.3% coupon' maps to the legitimate 9.25% ComputeCo notes due 2030 (B+ HY, not a penalty rate) — and the NEWER ComputeCo 2 notes priced TIGHTER at 6.75%, i.e. cost of capital is improving, the opposite of distress pricing. So the leverage/refi/carry signatures are firing on phantom notional. The REAL fragility is different and genuine but smaller: (1) severe cash burn — Q3 FY26 net loss $100.9M, 6-mo operating cash flow -$97.9M, TTM FCF margin reported near -500% as a heavy capex build-out runs ahead of revenue; (2) revenue/counterparty concentration — CoreWeave is ~69-70% of the ~$16B contracted backlog and the dominant near-term tenant, and CoreWeave is itself a leveraged, Microsoft-concentrated credit, so this is a daisy-chained AI-infra exposure; (3) project-finance opacity — debt sits in ringfenced SPVs (APLD ComputeCo LLC / ComputeCo 2 LLC) with parent completion guarantees, so headline net leverage understates contingent funding obligations to finish ELN-02/03 and Polaris Forge 2. Net: APLD is a high-burn, concentration-exposed, capital-markets-dependent developer, NOT a $27B over-levered balance-sheet bomb. Confirm-not-reject on a moderate, idiosyncratic basis; reject the $26.75B/$9.30B leverage thesis as an artifact.

findings.entity: Lumen Technologies, Inc. (LUMN; CIK 0000018926)
findings.fragility_thesis: REJECT the headline fragility flag as largely a data artifact, but the entity is a genuine, ALREADY-RESTRUCTURED high-yield credit — fragile in the past tense, stabilizing now. The scan's $91.19B gross debt is wrong by ~5x: actual consolidated long-term debt was ~$17.35B at YE2025 and ~$13B by Q1 2026 (vs ~$1B cash; net debt ~$16.4B → ~$12B). The $91B almost certainly double/triple-counts FACE/notional across the multi-issuer historical stack (Lumen HoldCo, Level 3 Financing, Qwest Corporation, Qwest Capital Funding, Embarq, legacy CenturyLink) PLUS tranches already refinanced, exchanged, or retired in the March-2024 TSA and the 2025-26 tender/exchange waves — a notional over-count, not a real obligation. The real story: Lumen already did a distressed, broad-creditor uptier exchange (TSA, completed Mar-2024) covering >$15B of debt, pushing the 2025-27 maturity wall down to ~$800M and extending maturities to 2029+. It then sold the consumer FTTH business to AT&T for $5.75B cash (closed Feb-2026), applying ~$4.8B to debt paydown and cutting net leverage from ~4.9x to ~3.9x aEBITDA. FY2025: ~$12.3B revenue (declining ~4% YoY), Adj. EBITDA at high end of $3.2-3.4B, FCF ~$1.04B (ex special items). It funds ~$1B+ of interest and is deleveraging, NOT bleeding out. The mispricing risk is the OPPOSITE of the flag: the credit was re-rated as a turnaround, and the AI/PCF backlog ($8.5B+ signed with Microsoft/AWS/Google/Meta, +$2.5B PCF in 2025) is largely hyperscaler-prepaid construction cash IN, not circular financing OUT.

findings.entity: Sarepta Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ: SRPT)
findings.fragility_thesis:
The scan flagged Sarepta on the wrong axis. The debt-driven flags are largely a DATA ARTIFACT and the front-loaded refi-wall hypothesis is REJECTED; the REAL fragility is a clinical/commercial demand collapse in the Elevidys gene-therapy franchise.

DEBT ARTIFACT: Scan's ~$6.66B gross / ~$5.33B near-term debt is a 3-4x over-count of the same convertible notes rolled forward through 2025 exchange transactions. Reality: the original $1.0B 1.25% 2027 convertibles were exchanged in Aug-2025 (~$700M) and Dec-2025 (~$291.4M) into new 4.875% convertible notes due 2030. Post-exchange stack = ~$158.6M of 2027 notes (the only ≤2027 maturity) + ~$893.4M of new 2030 notes = ~$1.05B principal (~$1.26B carrying value per Q3-2025). The scan appears to have summed the original issuance, each exchange's surrendered notional, and each newly-issued tranche as separate obligations. The 4.9% 'max coupon' is simply the new 2030 note rate (4.875%) — NOT a penalty/distressed coupon. The 'refi wall <=2027' is ~$159M, not $5B, and management has already termed it out to 2030. Leverage is modest: ~$1.05B debt against $2.20B FY2025 revenue and a still-cash-generative PMO franchise.

REAL FRAGILITY (operational, not balance-sheet): Elevidys suffered 3 patient deaths from acute liver failure (2 non-ambulatory DMD teens + 1 LGMD adult on the shared AAVrh74 vector). FDA forced a July-2025 US shipment pause + clinical holds, then a boxed warning for acute liver injury/failure and REMOVAL of the non-ambulatory indication (Nov-2025). Result: Elevidys revenue cratered — Q1-2026 $102M vs $375M Q1-2025 (down ~73% YoY). FY2025 swung to a GAAP net loss of $(713.4)M (vs +$235.2M in 2024); cash + investments fell from $1.50B (YE2024) to $0.95B (YE2025); 500-person layoff and CEO departure. The franchise's single highest-value asset is structurally impaired by safety, and the legacy PMO drugs (~$966M, facing competition/loss-of-exclusivity over time) now carry the company.

NET READ: This is NOT a leverage/refinancing fragility story. It is a moderate-severity demand/safety-impairment story with adequate near-term liquidity (~$0.95B cash vs ~$159M near-term maturity) but a deteriorating cash burn trajectory and a damaged growth driver. Solvency is not imminently at risk; the equity-/credit-relevant question is whether the de-rated Elevidys plus eroding PMO base can keep the company cash-flow-positive (management's 2026 claim) while the ~$1.05B convertible stack sits out to 2027/2030.

findings.entity: Global Net Lease, Inc. (NYSE: GNL) — CIK 0001526113
findings.fragility_thesis: REJECT the headline flag as a DATA ARTIFACT, but a genuine, MODERATE and already-known fragility remains. The scan's $38.56B gross / $39B footprint and ~$14.59B near-term are wrong by ~10-15x: GNL's actual gross principal debt was ~$2.6B at YE2025 (down from ~$4.7-5.0B at YE2024 / ~$5.2B peak post-RTL merger). The inflated figure almost certainly aggregates undrawn facility CAPACITY (the $1.5B multi-currency revolver), multi-currency notional, and/or double-counted draw+repay flows across periods rather than period-end outstanding balances. The '4.3% max coupon' is likewise an artifact: GNL's WEIGHTED-AVERAGE rate is ~4.2% (YE2025), so the parser captured a portfolio average and mislabeled it a max coupon — the actual rate range runs higher (mortgages + the 3.75% 2027 unsecured notes); coupons of 4.3% are not GNL's ceiling. Net of the artifact, the REAL fragility is ordinary mid-cap-REIT credit stress, fully telegraphed: (1) a 2025 dividend cut from $1.42 to $1.10/sh to redirect ~$74M/yr to deleveraging; (2) a FY2025 GAAP net loss of ~$(269.2)M driven by disposition losses/impairments on a ~$3.4B asset-sale program, not by operating shortfall; (3) elevated 6.7x net-debt/Adj. EBITDA and THIN interest coverage ~2.9x; (4) a 2027/2028/2029 fixed-rate maturity wall, with the 3.75% Dec-2027 $500M senior notes a near-term refi item; (5) thin 2026 AFFO/dividend coverage guided to ~108%. OFFSETS that argue against acute distress: ~$962M available liquidity, 97% occupancy, 98% fixed-rate, no major maturities until 2027, active deleveraging that improved leverage from 7.6x to 6.7x, and an improving rating trajectory (S&P/Fitch). Verdict: NOT mispriced as a hidden cliff; this is a deleveraging-but-stabilizing, investment-grade-adjacent net-lease REIT. The fired signatures (leverage 0.80, refi 0.38, concentration 0.24, hidden 0.20) are driven by the corrupted size inputs and should be down-weighted; on corrected fundamentals GNL is moderate-fragility, not a canary.

findings.entity: X Holdings Corp. / X Corp. (formerly Twitter; now a subsidiary within xAI, itself absorbed into SpaceX as of Feb 2026)
findings.fragility_thesis: The scan flagged X as a leveraged, front-loaded-refi-wall canary with a suspiciously cheap 2.0% coupon. On its own cash flows X IS genuinely fragile — but NOT for the reasons the scan encoded, and the standalone fragility is being actively rescued at the parent level, so the net mispricing is small and shrinking. THREE corrections: (1) The 2.0% coupon is a DATA ARTIFACT. X/xAI debt actually prices at ~12-12.5% fixed and SOFR+700-725bp floating — distressed-adjacent HY, not cheap paper. Any model treating this as 2% cost-of-debt has the sign of the risk inverted. (2) The ~$20B / 'all due <=2027' figure conflates entities and vintages. X's own buyout debt was ~$13B (2022), already fully sold off banks' books at 97-98c by April 2025 (a turnaround, not a fire sale); post-March-2025 xAI merger the combined entity carries ~$12B legacy-X debt plus xAI's ~$5B June-2025 raise = ~$17.5B — which is xAI/SpaceX-level debt, not 'X Holdings Corp.' standalone. (3) The 'refi wall' is being DEFUSED, not approached: in March 2026 Morgan Stanley notified lenders that X/xAI intend to repay the full ~$17.5B (redeeming the $3B bonds at ~117c) ahead of the SpaceX IPO, funded off the ~$1.25T SpaceX balance sheet. Standalone, X cannot service ~$12B at 12% — ~$2.7-2.9B revenue, ~$1.25B adj. EBITDA (achieved only via ~80% headcount cut), >$1B/yr cash interest => EBITDA/interest barely ~1.0-1.25x, negligible runway. That is the real fragility. But because X is now a sub of xAI/SpaceX and the debt is being voluntarily retired at a premium, the standalone insolvency risk is structurally backstopped. CONCLUSION: confirm intrinsic standalone fragility (high leverage, expensive debt, thin coverage) but REJECT the scan's specific canary framing — the cheap-coupon flag is spurious, the refi wall is being paid off, and the credit now lives inside a trillion-dollar private parent. Severity is moderate (intrinsic) but the live, tradeable fragility is low.

findings.entity: Oracle Corporation (NYSE: ORCL; CIK 0001341439)
findings.fragility_thesis: Oracle is NOT a near-term solvency canary on its own legacy cash flows — it is investment-grade (Moody's Baa2 / S&P BBB), generated ~$32B operating cash flow in FY2026, and has a manageable near-term maturity wall. The fragility is forward-looking and second-order: Oracle is borrowing aggressively (~$43B of new debt in FY2026, plan for ~$40B more in FY2027) to pre-fund $55.7B/yr of data-center capex AGAINST a $638B RPO backlog that is >50% concentrated in a single, deeply loss-making counterparty (OpenAI, burning ~$14-27B in 2026 and dependent on external funding). This converts a self-funding software franchise into a leveraged, single-counterparty infrastructure bet. The transmission mechanism: if OpenAI slows, renegotiates, or cannot fund ~$60B/yr of Oracle compute purchases, Oracle is left having raised ~$80-100B of debt and built dedicated GPU capacity against revenue that does not arrive — collapsing the RPO-to-revenue conversion that justifies the leverage. The scan's 'circular financing' flag is legitimate (Nvidia->OpenAI->Oracle compute loop). The seed gross-debt figure ($112.61B) and 4.8% max coupon are REAL but STALE mid-FY2026 snapshots; by year-end debt is materially higher and incremental coupons reach 6.1%+. Severity is elevated but the timing is multi-year, not imminent — Oracle has IG market access and a long-dated debt profile as a shock absorber. This is a 'pre-spend ahead of demand' fragility, not a liquidity-cliff fragility.

findings.entity: Sabre Corporation (NASDAQ: SABR) / Sabre GLBL Inc. (debt issuer)
findings.fragility_thesis: REAL fragility, but the scan's HEADLINE NUMBERS ARE A DATA ARTIFACT and must be rejected before judging it. (1) GROSS DEBT ARTIFACT: scan says ~$15.88B gross / ~$8.12B near-term (≤2027). Actual gross debt is ~$4.2B net of costs/discounts (~$4.4B face) at YE2025, down from ~$5.1B at YE2024. The ~3x overcount almost certainly comes from summing 2025's SERIAL exchange/tender/refinancing transaction notionals — Sabre ran multiple exchange offers + a $1.325B new-notes issue + term-loan refis in 2025, so the SAME underlying principal got counted across each exchanged/re-issued leg. The '$8.12B ≤2027' figure is the same artifact: after refinancing, >90% of debt now matures 2029+, with only ~$378M of 2027 notes (8.625% ~$332M + 11.25% stub ~$46M) genuinely near-term, plus a small 2026 exchangeable. So leverage/refi/carry signatures fired on phantom principal. (2) WHAT IS REAL: on a CASH-FLOW basis Sabre is genuinely stressed. Net leverage ~7x on Adjusted EBITDA of $536M; net debt ~$3.74B. Interest expense ~$448M EXCEEDS operating income ~$295M; Adjusted EBITDA $536M covers cash interest only ~1.2x. FY2025 FCF was NEGATIVE ~$192M (vs -$9M in 2024). FY2025 net income of $525M is a NON-OPERATING one-off (gain on the $1.1B / ~$960M-net Hospitality Solutions divestiture, July 2025) — do not read it as earnings power. Stockholders' deficit ~-$1.0B is LBO/goodwill legacy, not a fresh distress signal. (3) COUPON: max coupon ~11.25%/11.125% is REAL but is a primary-market high-yield rate for a single-B/CCC issuer in a VOLUNTARY refi (new 11.125% notes due 2030 issued ~at par June 2025), NOT a penalty/default rate and NOT a distressed secondary trading discount — so the '11.2% distressed-priced tranche' seed hypothesis is largely FALSE-flag. NET READ: this is a high-but-stabilizing-leverage credit that bought itself runway by terming out the maturity wall to 2029+ and selling a division; the fragility is thin coupon coverage and negative FCF, not an imminent maturity cliff. Mid-tier severity at most — NOT a canary, NOT mispriced as the $15.88B/$8.12B inputs would suggest.

findings.entity: Bausch Health Companies Inc. (NYSE/TSX: BHC) [CIK 0000885590]
findings.fragility_thesis: The scan's headline ($32.29B gross / $18B due <=2027 / 11% coupon / circular financing) is materially STALE and partially a consolidation/refi artifact. Reality as of Q1 2026: consolidated total debt is ~$20.4-20.8B (long-term debt and other = $20.764B at 3/31/2026), NOT $32B. Of that, ~$4.6B is BLCO debt that is consolidated for accounting (88% stake) but is non-recourse to the BHC stub (BLCO has its own credit agreement and was designated an unrestricted subsidiary in Nov 2022). The recourse RemainCo debt is roughly $15-16B. The $32B figure double-counts pre-refinancing principal and/or BLCO debt — a real data artifact. The '$18B refi wall <=2027' is largely RESOLVED: two 2025 refinancings totaling ~$9.6B (including a $4.0-4.4B 10.00% notes-due-2032 issue and a $1.6B Dec-2025 exchange) pushed maturities out so that <$700M remains through 2027; the wall now sits in 2028-2032. The 11.0% coupon is REAL but being retired — the ~$1.77B 11.00% Senior Secured Notes due 2028 were exchanged into new 10.00% notes due 2032. The 'circular/related-party' flag maps to the legitimate ~$2.2B intercompany note and 88% BLCO ownership structure, not fraudulent circular financing. So three of four seed hypotheses are downgraded. THE GENUINE FRAGILITY THAT REMAINS: (1) Leverage is still ~6.5x net debt/EBITDA (~$20B net debt vs ~$3.1B consolidated adj. EBITDA; stub EBITDA ~$2.7B), deep junk (Moody's Caa2, S&P CCC/CCC+). (2) Coupons on new money are ~10% — refinancing is happening at distressed rates, so each term-out raises cash interest (interest expense rose to $1.604B in 2025, +$216M YoY) and erodes the very FCF used to deleverage. (3) The earnings engine has a hard structural deadline: Xifaxan (largest product, ~$1.6-2B revenue, Salix segment) faces authorized/settled generic entry from Teva/Sun/Sandoz in Jan 2028, and the Phase 3 RED-C trial to expand the label FAILED in Jan 2026, removing the key offset. A $1.4B impairment was booked in Q1 2026. So this is a real, slow-moving deleveraging-vs-patent-cliff race, not an imminent default. Solvency depends on (a) continued refi access at ~10%, and (b) monetizing the BLCO stake (worth multiples of the stub's market cap) before the 2028 Xifaxan cliff bites. NOT an imminent canary; it is a chronically-stressed, already-distressed-rated credit whose fragility is correctly real but whose magnitude was overstated ~1.6x by the scan.

findings.entity: Goldman Sachs BDC, Inc. (GSBD) [CIK 0001572694]
findings.fragility_thesis: The scan's headline flags are a DATA ARTIFACT and must be rejected: GSBD's own balance-sheet debt is ~$1.92B (10-Q, 3/31/2026), not $22.6B — a ~12x overcount. The "$22.6B gross / $10.13B near-term" figure almost certainly comes from summing the underlying portfolio-company loan principal in the Schedule of Investments (debt investments are listed at ~233% of net assets, i.e. ~$3.2B of fund assets, with per-company facility notionals and commitments double-counted), not GSBD's senior securities. The 'leverage 0.69 / refi 0.45 / hidden 0.44' signatures inherit that error. CORRECTED real debt stack: $720.5M secured revolver (matures 6/24/2030) + $400M 6.375% 2027 Notes (3/11/2027) + $400M 5.10% 2029 Notes + $400M 5.65% 2030 Notes = $1.9205B. Near-term maturity wall is therefore essentially the single $400M 2027 note, not a $10B cliff — refi risk is LOW (revolver runs to 2030, 62.5% unsecured, investment-grade). HOWEVER, GSBD is independently and genuinely deteriorating on credit quality, which the artifact-driven flags happened to mask rather than measure: non-accruals rose to 3.2% of FV / 4.7% of cost (11 names, up from 9); NII/share collapsed from $0.37 (Q4'25) to $0.22 (Q1'26), yield-on-book 11.7%->7.2%; net realized loss ~$21.6M and a $13.6M net-asset decrease drove NAV from $12.64 to $12.17; net debt/equity rose to 1.37x; asset-coverage cushion thinned to 171% (vs 150% regulatory floor). Base dividend $0.32/qtr now exceeds $0.22 NII — coverage is broken and supplemental dividends are at risk. Fitch revised the BBB- IDR outlook to NEGATIVE (May 2026). Net read: the entity is NOT a hidden $22B leverage bomb; it is a regulated, IG-rated BDC with a real but bounded credit-quality slide. Fragility is moderate and idiosyncratic (middle-market credit cycle / dividend cut), not systemic or capital-structure-driven.

findings.entity: Enbridge Inc (NYSE/TSX: ENB; CIK 0000895728)
findings.fragility_thesis: REJECT the fragility flag. This is a beam, not a canary. Enbridge is an investment-grade, regulated/contracted toll-road business whose cash flows are structurally insulated from commodity price and volume risk: ~95-98% of adjusted EBITDA is cost-of-service or take-or-pay (paid on capacity availability, not throughput or commodity price), and >80% has built-in inflation pass-through. FY2025 adjusted EBITDA was ~C$19.95B with DCF ~C$12.45B; the dividend (~C$3.88/sh, 31st consecutive annual raise) runs at a 60-70% DCF payout, leaving multi-billion retained DCF to self-fund equity. Net-debt/adjusted-EBITDA is 4.8x, squarely inside management's own 4.5-5.0x target and the rating-agency tolerance for a regulated pipeline. Every fired signature is explainable as the normal shape of a large regulated utility, not latent distress: (1) leverage 0.87 / large $55B footprint — true gross debt is actually LARGER than the scan saw (long-term debt ~C$75B as of Q3'25 vs scan's $54.7B), but it is term, laddered, fixed-rate, and IG-rated, supported by a rate base, not fragile; the scan understated debt by capturing only a subset (likely the US-registered note tranche / a USD-denominated cut), so the absolute figure is a partial-parse artifact rather than evidence of hidden leverage. (2) refi 0.49 / near-term ~$26.65B — a continuous-issuer maturity ladder; ENB terms out maturities routinely (e.g., US$1.5B Nov-2025, US$2B and multiple 424B5 issues through 2025) and has large committed bank liquidity; refinancing access for a single-A-to-BBB+ regulated pipeline is not a stress point at current leverage. (3) concentration HHI 0.51 — reflects regulated/long-term-contract counterparties (utilities, IG shippers, Mainline customers under the 2024-approved tolling settlement to 2028), the OPPOSITE of fragility because revenue is contracted/regulated regardless of any single shipper's volumes. (4) circular/related-party 0.30 — explained by the upstream/downstream cross-guarantee structure between Enbridge Inc. and wholly-owned former-MLP subsidiaries EEP and SEP (rolled up 2018-2019); these are credit-ENHANCING unconditional guarantees that consolidate the obligor group, not circular financing. (5) max coupon 7.4% — consistent with a hybrid/subordinated note or a higher-rate vintage tranche, not a penalty/default rate. The only genuine, modest fragilities are structural for the sector: elevated absolute leverage that leaves limited headroom for a sustained EBITDA shock or a rating-agency methodology change, exposure to the Mainline tolling re-set after 2028, and large ongoing capex (~C$10-11B/yr) that keeps the entity a perennial net issuer dependent on continued capital-market access. None of these is a near-term solvency threat.
findings.false_positive_reason: All five fired signatures reproduce exactly from size/ladder/structural formulas with zero genuine distress content. The composite (0.460, rank #3) is dominated by size proxies — leverage (0.22) + refi (0.18) = 40% of weight — which mechanically score any large continuous IG issuer high regardless of solvency. Specifically: leverage=0.87 is log10(notional)/2, a size proxy with no leverage ratio; refi=0.49 is a normal laddered-maturity continuous-issuer shape; carry=0.24 comes from a subordinated/hybrid note coupon, not stress pricing; concentration=0.51 is a sparse-sample artifact over only 6 named counterparties for a contracted/regulated toll road; circular=0.30 is a mechanical floor with related_party_flags=0, reflecting the credit-enhancing EEP/SEP guarantor structure. distress=0.0. findings.entity: Cannae Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: CNNE), CIK 0001704720

findings.entity: MFA Financial, Inc. (NYSE: MFA) — CIK 0001055160
findings.fragility_thesis: REJECT the scan's distress flag — the load-bearing inputs are data artifacts. findings.entity: Omnicom Group Inc. (NYSE: OMC), CIK 0000029989 — global advertising/marketing holding company; CIK 0000029989
findings.fragility_thesis: NOT FRAGILE — the flag is a debt-magnitude DATA ARTIFACT, not a real fragility. The scan's $27.51B gross / $18.78B near-term figures are a ~2.7x overcount of an entity whose actual gross debt is ~$10.2B (Q1 2026) and net debt only ~$5.69B (FY2025). The most likely artifact mechanics: (1) double-counting the November 2025 IPG note exchange — Omnicom issued ~$2.76B of NEW notes that REPLACED ~$2.76B of legacy IPG notes; a naive parser sums both the old and new legs plus the full $2.95B exchange-offer notional; (2) counting undrawn facility CAPACITY as drawn debt — the $3.5B revolving credit facility (undrawn) and $3.0B commercial-paper program backstop; (3) summing gross notional across the full history of note issuances/redemptions without netting matured/refinanced tranches (e.g., the 3.65% 2024 notes, the 3.60% April-2026 notes retired, etc.). The '$18.78B due <=2027 refi wall' is internally impossible: total consolidated debt is only ~$10B and the FIRST near-term maturity is not until July 2027 (€500M 0.80% notes), with the stack staggered out to 2048. On its own cash flows, OMC is comfortably solvent: FY2025 revenue $17.3B, adjusted EBITA $2.7B (15.6% margin), leverage 2.5x EBITDA against a 3.5x covenant, $4.3B cash + $3.5B undrawn revolver. The 5.3% 'max coupon' is genuine but is ordinary investment-grade (Baa1/BBB+) pricing on 2034/2036 paper — NOT a penalty/distress rate. The 'concentration 0.10' and 'circular 0.30' signatures are also rejected on substance (see below). Real but non-solvency-threatening risks are confined to IPG integration execution (a $1.5B synergy target, $1.1B+ FY2025 severance/repositioning charges that depressed GAAP operating income to $444.7M, ~$3,200 IPG job cuts), +~$200M 2026 interest from acquired IPG debt, and secular decline in traditional advertising. SEVERITY = LOW, driven entirely by integration/secular factors, not by the balance sheet the scan flagged.

findings.entity: ADAMAS TRUST, INC. (Nasdaq: ADAM; CIK 0001273685) — formerly New York Mortgage Trust, Inc. (NYMT), rebranded Sept 3, 2025
findings.fragility_thesis: REJECT the headline fragility flag — it is overwhelmingly a mortgage-REIT structural artifact, not corporate distress. The "~$6.18B gross debt" is short-term REPO/warehouse financing ($6.75B at 12/31/25) collateralized by a $10.5B leveraged Agency-RMBS/credit securities portfolio; this is the firm's normal operating model, marked-to-market and self-liquidating, NOT term corporate leverage. A further $3.51B of consolidated CDO/securitization debt is explicitly NON-RECOURSE to the parent (the scan's "0 SPV/non-recourse flags" is wrong — the 10-K is full of consolidated VIEs/securitizations). The "max 9.9% coupon" is the 9.875% Senior Notes due 2030 — a small Nasdaq-listed baby-bond COUPON near par, not a distressed PRICE. True corporate unsecured debt is tiny: only $360.4M senior unsecured notes + $45M subordinated debentures (~$405M, ~3.6% of the $11.2B liability stack, well-covered by $1.43B equity and $206.5M cash). FY2025 was a recovery year: net income ~$101M (vs a 2024 loss), interest income +50%, GAAP book value +3.4% to $9.60, dividend raised 15%, and the company refinanced notes + extended buybacks (capital-markets access, not distress). The genuine, but ordinary-for-the-sector, fragilities are: (1) ~5.0x recourse leverage exposing book value to RMBS spread/rate moves and repo margin calls, and (2) repo rollover/counterparty dependence. Net: a normally-functioning leveraged mortgage REIT, mildly rate/spread-sensitive, NOT a mispriced credit canary.

findings.entity: Cheniere Energy Partners, L.P. (CQP) — CIK 0001383650

findings.entity: Entergy Louisiana, LLC (ELC) — CIK 0001348952
findings.fragility_thesis: REJECT the fragility flag — it is overwhelmingly a data artifact, not a credit story. The scan's "$67.49B gross debt" is impossible for this entity and roughly 4-7x the real number: Entergy Louisiana's actual externally-held debt is ~$9.35B of Collateral Trust Mortgage Bonds (6/30/2025), plus non-recourse storm-recovery securitization SPE bonds (~$3B range) and modest other debt — realistic total long-term debt is on the order of $15-18B. For scale, the ENTIRE Entergy Corporation parent (all five utility opcos combined) carries only ~$28-30B total debt and ~$11.9B annual revenue, so a single state opco cannot carry $67B. The figure almost certainly came from naively summing every debt notional across shelf registrations, redeemed/refinanced series, internal collateral bonds, and securitization SPEs in EDGAR exhibits. The 'circular/related-party financing' flag (sig 0.30) is the $6,750M 'ELL Class A Bonds' issued under the ELL Mortgage that are PLEDGED AS COLLATERAL to secure the Collateral Trust Mortgage Bonds — a standard first-mortgage collateral mechanism, not leverage; counting them as separate debt double-counts ~$6.75B. S&P rates ELL BBB+ stable; the entity is a rate-regulated monopoly with guaranteed cost recovery and is operating normally (parent reported 2025 results 'in top half of guidance range,' Feb 2026). This is a beam, not a canary: low intrinsic fragility, the strong load-bearing member, not a fault line.

findings.entity: Bain Capital Specialty Finance, Inc. (BCSF) — CIK 0001655050; externally managed, non-diversified BDC (RIC) advised by BCSF Advisors, LP (Bain Capital Credit)
findings.fragility_thesis: REJECT the seed flags — this entity is NOT fragile and is NOT mispriced on its own cash flows. The economy-wide scan's headline numbers are data artifacts of BDC structure, not real obligations. (1) The "$11.25B gross / $4.15B near-term debt" is a ~7.7x overcount: BCSF's ACTUAL total principal debt is ~$1.47B (Q1 2026, 3/31/26), with debt/equity 1.34x and net leverage 1.28x — squarely within the 2:1 BDC regulatory cap and at the upper end of its own 1.0–1.25x target. The $11.25B almost certainly sums revolver COMMITMENTS/capacity (~$660M undrawn alone) plus the NOTIONAL DEBT OF THE 212 UNDERLYING PORTFOLIO BORROWERS visible in the schedule of investments — i.e., it is counting BCSF's assets (loans it OWNS) as if they were BCSF's liabilities. Those are non-recourse to BCSF. (2) The 'concentration HHI 0.64 / 7 SPV-non-recourse flags' is the BDC's own ring-fenced financing architecture (Sumitomo SMBC revolver, BCC Middle Market CLO 2019-1 securitization, unsecured notes) — standard, investment-grade-rated, bankruptcy-remote SPV plumbing, NOT hidden leverage. Real BORROWER concentration is the opposite of concentrated: largest single position ~40bps, 212 companies, 30 industries. The 0.64 HHI is measuring instrument-type homogeneity (everything is a senior secured loan) or financier concentration (the Sumitomo facility), neither of which is an economic concentration risk. But NII of $0.42 FULLY covers the $0.42 dividend (1.0x coverage, 10% annualized ROE), non-accruals are very low (0.6% fair value / 1.4% cost) and improving, 66% first-lien, weighted cost of debt 4.6%, 4.1-yr avg maturity, $729M liquidity. findings.entity: Meta Platforms, Inc. (META) [CIK 0001326801]
findings.fragility_thesis: NOT FRAGILE on its own cash flows — the seed flags are stale/artifactual and the entity is net-cash with overwhelming coverage. The economy-wide scan's inputs ($29B gross debt, 4.9% max coupon) reflect Meta's PRE-November-2025 balance sheet (the 2022/2023/2024 issuances). On 11/3/2025 Meta priced a $30B six-tranche senior-notes deal, roughly doubling the stack to ~$59B principal / ~$58.7B carrying. Even post-doubling: $81.6B cash+marketable securities exceeds gross debt (NET CASH), FY2025 operating cash flow was $115.8B, net income $60.5B, free cash flow ~$43.6B, and interest expense was only ~$1.165B (coverage ~71x). The "leverage 0.74" and "refi 0.57" signatures are mechanical size/maturity-bucket artifacts that ignore the asset side. findings.entity: Eastman Kodak Co (NYSE: KODK; CIK 0000031235)
findings.fragility_thesis: REJECT the headline flag as a DATA ARTIFACT, but note the underlying story is a REAL canary that already fired and was cured. The scan's ~$2.34B "gross debt" is NOT financial debt — Kodak's actual financial debt at YE2025 was ~$200M term loan + ~$99-102M Series B mandatorily-redeemable preferred = ~$300M, against ~$337M unrestricted cash, i.e. a NET-CASH position. The $2.34B figure almost certainly swept in the gross KRIP pension benefit obligation/plan liabilities (the terminated plan held ~$1.0B+ of EXCESS assets on a multi-billion gross base), plus likely the cash-collateralized LC facility notional and RPA receivables — classic gross-pension/notional double-count. The genuine fragility was the May 22, 2026 maturity wall (term loan + $99M 4% Series B preferred + LC facility all due) that produced a substantial-doubt going-concern disclosure through mid-2025. That risk was RESOLVED: the Dec 2, 2025 pension reversion delivered ~$767M of excess assets (~$609M cash), ~$312M of which prepaid the term loan to $200M; the term loan maturity was extended to Aug 15, 2028 and the preferred refinanced into 6% Series B redeemable June 2029. Going-concern doubt was formally removed. By Q1 2026 total borrowings were ~$160M and cash ~$399M. Net: this entity is NOT currently fragile on a cash-vs-obligations basis. It is thinly profitable (FY2025 op-EBITDA only $62M on $1.069B revenue; Q1 2026 net loss $16M), so it is a low-margin survivor, not a distressed credit. The 12.5% coupon is real but on a small, now-shrinking facility and is structured 7.5% cash + 5.0% PIK (a financing-cost signal, not a penalty/default rate).
findings.false_positive_reason: The $2.337B/$1.275B "gross debt" headline that drives the flag is a data artifact — a gross KRIP pension-obligation/notional sweep (plus likely the cash-collateralized LC notional and RPA receivables) double-counted as financial debt. Actual financial debt is ~$300M against $337M cash (net cash). The carry (0.75) and hidden-leverage (0.75) signature scores are inflated by that mis-extracted base. The genuine canary — the May 2026 maturity wall and the substantial-doubt going-concern disclosure — was real but already fired in 2025 and was cured by the Nov 2025 pension reversion, the term-loan paydown/extension, and the March 2026 Series B amendment, with going-concern doubt formally removed.

findings.entity: MGM Resorts International (NYSE: MGM, CIK 0000789570)

Coverage is comfortable today: interest expense only ~$419M, cash ~$2.1B, BetMGM now cash-distributing (~$135M in 2025), and management repurchased ~$1.2B of stock in 2025 — capital-return behavior inconsistent with distress.

findings.entity: Ares Capital Corporation (NASDAQ: ARCC) — CIK 0001287750
findings.fragility_thesis: REJECT the fragility flag. This is a confirm-or-reject task and ARCC confirms as one of the most conservatively levered, best-dividend-covered BDCs, not a fragile entity. Coverage is robust: core EPS $2.01 vs $1.92 dividend (20+ consecutive quarters covered), portfolio interest coverage 2.2x, non-accruals 1.8% at cost / 1.2% at FV (well under the 2.8% post-GFC and 3.8% BDC averages). findings.entity: Navient Corp (NAVI; CIK 0001593538)
findings.fragility_thesis: REJECT the headline flag as largely a data artifact, with a residual but contained real weakness. (1) The "$157.28B gross debt" is ~3.5x Navient's actual ~$45.7B total balance-sheet debt — it almost certainly double/triple-counts the notional of dozens of SEPARATELY SEC-registered Navient student-loan ABS trusts (NSLT/NAVRL/NAVEL series, plus legacy SLM trusts like the JSM ticker that even surfaced as a "10-K filer"). Each trust files its own 10-D/424B; summing trust-level notes across filings inflates the figure. (2) "Concentration HHI 1.00 / 3 counterparties" is also artifactual: a securitization sponsor's filing-level 'counterparties' are its own trusts and indenture trustees, not customer concentration. Real exposure is a granular pool of millions of student-loan borrowers — the OPPOSITE of concentrated. (3) The 9.4% 'distressed' coupon is the 9.375% Senior Notes due 2031, which Navient SUCCESSFULLY publicly issued $500M of in May 2026 — direct evidence the unsecured market is OPEN, which negates the refi-stress thesis. The genuine residual fragility: Navient is Ba3/BB-/BB-, posted a FY2025 GAAP net loss of ~$80M on rising private-loan credit costs (90+ DPD delinquencies ~$2.5B vs $1.9B; Q3 private-loan provision jumped to $155M), and runs a shrinking equity base (~4.9% GAAP equity/assets, ~9.1% adjusted tangible). This is fragile as an equity/earnings story, not a near-term solvency or credit-cascade story.

findings.entity: HIGH STREET CAPITAL PARTNERS, LLC (operating-company borrower / Up-C subsidiary of Acreage Holdings, Inc.; "HSCP d/b/a Acreage Holdings")
findings.fragility_thesis: REAL distress, but already realized and resolved — not a live mispricing and not a clean data artifact. The scan flagged a borrower NAME ("HIGH STREET CAPITAL PARTNERS, LLC") with no CIK/ticker, single source, single counterparty (HHI=1.0), nonrecourse flag, ~$0.20B notional, 20% max coupon. Identity resolution: HSCP is the operating subsidiary/Up-C borrower of public registrant Acreage Holdings, Inc. (CIK 0001762359); the LLC name appears as borrower on the Dec 16, 2021 credit agreement with AFC Agent LLC / VRT Agent LLC (parent Acreage as guarantor — hence the legitimate nonrecourse/HHI=1.0 flags). Acreage WAS genuinely distressed: FY2024 going-concern qualification, Q1-2024 default on its Prime-rate facilities (all debt reclassed to current), and emergency financing including a $15M bridge at ~60% and an earlier $70M term loan at 15%. So the credit was real high-cost cannabis paper, and the 20% scan coupon, if anything, UNDERSTATES the worst rate (60% bridge). HOWEVER: (1) the ~$200M notional is stale/over-counted vs. net — at 6/30/2024 total debt was ~$261.8M of which the A&R High Street/AFC-VRT facility was ~$144.8M (facility A&R'd to ~US$167M); the $200M likely conflates facility plus other tranches at a particular filing snapshot. (2) The distress was resolved by ACQUISITION, not default: Canopy USA, LLC completed its takeover of Acreage on Dec 9, 2024 (delisted from CSE), contributed ~$70M cash to retire short-term debt, applied a $30M escrowed option premium, and restructured the remainder. The canary already fired (going concern + default in early 2024) and was absorbed into a parent. Forward-looking standalone fragility is now LOW because the entity is private, debt partially paid down, and credit-supported by Canopy. Verdict: CONFIRM the entity is/was distressed; REJECT it as a current live short/mispricing canary — the event is in the past and the equity outcome (take-under) is settled.
findings.false_positive_reason: As a CURRENT fragility/mispricing signal the record is principally a data artifact: (a) the distress-driving 'max_coupon 0.20' is a covenant ceiling on hypothetical future subordinated PIK debt, not the loan's actual 13.50% cash coupon — the scan extracted the largest 'X% per annum' string in the document; (b) the full $200.36M is booked as near_term_notional despite a Sept 13, 2027 maturity, inflating the refi/near-term signature; (c) the entity is a subsidiary borrower double-counted against the parent Canopy Growth record built from the very same exhibit, manufacturing a phantom standalone 'no-CIK, HHI=1.0 canary'; (d) the underlying distress event (going concern + 2024 default) is real but past-tense and was resolved by the Dec 2024 Canopy acquisition, so it is already-distressed-and-resolved rather than a live short.

findings.entity:
PennyMac Mortgage Investment Trust (Mortgage REIT, tier beam)
THESIS: PMT is a MODERATE, slow-bleed fragility — NOT the acute $53B/11.3%-distress profile the scan implied. Two of the seed hypotheses are data artifacts and should be rejected: (1) Gross debt is NOT ~$53.20B. PMT's FY2025 total LIABILITIES are ~$19.5B against ~$21.3B assets and ~$1.9B equity; the debt stack is ~$16.8B (repo ~$8.0B + asset-backed VIE financing ~$7.8B + unsecured notes ~$1.0B). The $53B figure is almost certainly a double/triple-count of repo notional rollovers, gross facility commitments, and overlapping maturity schedules — a classic mREIT artifact where short-term repo that rolls many times per year is summed as if term debt. (2) The 11.3% 'distressed' coupon is NOT a distressed bond. PMT's actual fixed unsecured coupons are 5.50% (2026 exchangeable), 8.50% (2029 exchangeable), 8.125%/8.00%/6.75% on Series A/B/C fixed-to-floating preferreds, plus public senior notes. ~11.3% is consistent with the ALL-IN floating rate (SOFR ~5.3% + ~4.19% spread) on a secured FMSR term note during the 2023-24 high-rate window, or a now-floating fixed-to-floating preferred — i.e., a market-clearing secured financing rate, not a penalty/distress signal. What IS real: (a) genuine COUNTERPARTY CONCENTRATION — ~44% of repo amount-at-risk (~$1.06B at risk on ~$6-8B repo) sits with a single counterparty, Atlas Securitized Products L.P. (Apollo-affiliated, the former Credit Suisse securitized-products book); loss of that line would force rapid deleveraging at adverse prices. (b) An EARNINGS/COVERAGE deterioration: ROE fell from 13% (Q4'25) to 4% (Q1'26), EPS from $0.48 to $0.16, while the dividend held at $0.40/qtr — meaning the common dividend is currently UNcovered on a Q1'26 run-rate, and book value is eroding ($15.87 YE24 -> $15.25 YE25 -> $14.98 Q1'26). The structural fragility is the standard mREIT one: rate/spread/prepayment sensitivity and rollover dependence, compounded by single-counterparty repo reliance and a fee-extracting external-manager governance model. But solvency is intact: 41% of debt is non-recourse VIE/securitization financing that ring-fences pool-level credit losses from the parent, liquidity/cash ~$214M, and the firm is actively terming out 2026 maturities. Net read: a rate-cycle-sensitive carry vehicle with a thinning dividend cushion, not a near-term default candidate. The scan's leverage (0.87) and refi (0.64) signatures fire on inflated inputs; the legitimately interesting vectors are concentration (Atlas) and the dividend-coverage gap.

findings.entity: NRG Energy, Inc. (NYSE: NRG; CIK 0001013871)
findings.fragility_thesis: REJECT the fragility flag — this is a scan data artifact, not a fragile credit. The "$86.5B gross debt / $14.78B near-term" figures are off by roughly 6-8x. findings.entity: Wynn Resorts, Limited (NASDAQ: WYNN; CIK 0001174922)

findings.entity: Blackstone Mortgage Trust, Inc. (BXMT) — CIK 0001061630
findings.fragility_thesis: REJECT the "fragile/hidden-leverage" framing as currently scored — but flag the scan's gross-debt number as materially wrong. The genuine fragility vector here is ASSET CREDIT (office CRE), which was real and acute in 2023-24 (office ~36% of book; Moody's cut CFR to Ba3 on office concerns; CECL reserve peaked ~$755M) — but it has been actively de-risked: office down to ~18% US / 6% non-US by YE2025, impaired loans cut ~96% from the Q3-2024 peak, CECL reserve down ~60% YoY to ~$284-296M, portfolio 98-99% performing, dividend ($0.47) covered three consecutive quarters by distributable EPS-before-realized-losses ($0.49). The mispricing, if any, is mild residual office tail risk and reliance on continued repayment velocity to fund new originations — not hidden leverage or imminent insolvency.

findings.entity: Ameris Bancorp (ABCB), CIK 0000351569 — regional bank holding company; bank subsidiary Ameris Bank
findings.fragility_thesis: NOT FRAGILE — the flag is a data artifact, REJECT. Ameris's actual non-deposit funding (the only thing that behaves like refinanceable debt) was just $611.3M at Q4 2025 (FHLB advances $423.7M + other borrowings $9.9M + subordinated debentures $134.0M), DOWN from $764.7M in 2024. Every fired signature (leverage 1.00, refi 0.82, carry 0.32, concentration 0.17) traces to deposits+notional being counted as debt against a thin equity sliver, which mechanically inflates 'leverage' and 'refi' for any bank.

The scan's "leverage/refi/carry/hidden" signatures and "20% tranche" are artifacts of misparsing the 2025 facility agreement.

findings.entity: American Water Works Company, Inc. (AWK) — CIK 0001410636, NYSE-listed regulated water/wastewater utility holding company
findings.fragility_thesis: REJECT the fragility flag — this is a false positive driven by data artifacts in the economy-wide scan. (1) The "$21.25B gross debt / $18.46B near-term wall" is materially wrong: the FY2025 10-K/press release shows long-term debt of $12,777M + short-term debt $1,588M = ~$14.4B total, and scheduled maturities of only $1,479M (2026) + $646M (2027) = ~$2.1B through 2027 — roughly one-ninth of the alleged $18.46B wall. The scan appears to have double-counted debt issued by the finance subsidiary (AWCC) against the parent and/or summed gross notional across overlapping entities/exhibits. (2) The "circular / related-party financing" signature is simply American Water Capital Corp. (AWCC), a wholly-owned, fully-disclosed finance conduit that issues virtually all group debt and on-lends to regulated operating subsidiaries under a support agreement — the standard utility-holdco financing structure, not a red flag. (3) The 5.2% max coupon is an ordinary 2036 senior note priced at market, not a penalty/default rate. On its own cash flows, AWK is among the LEAST fragile entities a scan could surface: monopoly franchise, recession-resistant essential-service demand, rate-base growth, and regulator-approved cost recovery. Coverage is comfortable (FY2025 EBITDA ~$2.74B vs interest expense $615M ≈ 4.5x; net income $1.11B), and it is investment-grade (S&P A / Moody's Baa1, stable). The only genuine forward item is the pending all-stock merger with Essential Utilities (WTRG) closing ~Q1 2027 (~$63B combined EV, ~$29.3B combined rate base) — accretive, equity-funded (no leverage spike), and it brings integration/regulatory-approval execution risk rather than solvency risk. findings.entity: TORONTO-DOMINION BANK (TD) [CIK 0000947263]
findings.fragility_thesis: REJECTED as flagged — this is a data artifact, not a fragile canary. Three independent mis-tags: (1) SECTOR WRONG: TD is a global systemically important BANK, not "Power / utility" (the bad tag likely bled from a Moody's headline that bundled "TD Bank downgrade" next to "CT gas utilities negative outlook"). (2) TIER WRONG: a "canary" is defined as small/obscure-fails-first; TD is a G-SIB, the opposite. (3) The load-bearing "19.1% distressed coupon" is NOT a credit spread — it is the embedded-derivative coupon on TD's retail MARKET-LINKED / AUTO-CALLABLE CONTINGENT-COUPON NOTES (Form 424B2). TD is among the most prolific issuers of these; confirmed live offerings carry 16.8%, 17.5%, even 23.85% contingent coupons, paid only if linked tech stocks stay above a ~50% barrier. That is option premium, not distress. TD's actual senior unsecured rating is Aa2/AA-; a 19.1% senior credit spread for an Aa2 issuer is economically impossible, which is itself proof the coupon is structured-note premium. The captured notional ($110M gross, $2.76M near-term, 11 deals) is a microscopic non-representative slice of a ~$1.3T-deposit, ~$2T-asset bank; leverage 0.0227 reflects the tiny captured-fragment denominator, and carry=1.0 / circular=true / counterparty_HHI=1.0 are all single-issuer-shelf artifacts (every note shares the TD issuer root). NET: no debt-coverage, refinancing, or liquidity fragility here. There IS a real, separate overhang — the Oct 2024 BSA/AML guilty plea (~$3.09B penalties) and a $434B OCC asset cap on TD's U.S. retail bank pending remediation — but that is an earnings/growth-cap and franchise-reputation issue at a profitable, deposit-funded, well-capitalized bank, NOT the distressed-tranche mechanism the scan fired on, and the scan did not actually detect it.
findings.false_positive_reason: Triple data artifact, all verified in-repo.
